newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA PROBES 5,000 FAKE DRIVER'S LICENCES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA PROBES 5,000 FAKE DRIVER'S LICENCES.

text.p: South Africa said on Wednesday that 5,000 false driver's licences were under investigation in the Gauteng region centered on Johannesburg.
The probe into fraudulently issued licences is also continuing in other regions, particularly KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga, police and transport officials said in a statement.

Flem Meyer, of the licencing inspectorate of the Department of Transport, said the "huge numbers" of drivers with fake licences were contributing to South Africa's unacceptably high road accident death tolls.

"Any issuing of fraudulent licences must be seen in the same light as murder," Meyer said. "Unskilled people are allowed to endanger the lives of law-abiding road users who take safety on our roads seriously."

Reports of a wide-ranging scam in the issuing of driver's and learner's licences were highlighted recently when deputy parliamentary speaker Baleka Kgositsile was implicated. She has denied the charge and a commission of inquiry in Mpumalanga is currently investigating the claims.
Transport Minister Mac Maharaj told a mini-debate in parliament earlier this month that the government planned to crack down on false licences issued by corrupt officials.

Maharaj said drivers will have to apply for new licences which will be issued in a new credit card format from March 1, 1998, with special features such as a water mark and security printing to discourage fraud.
From 1998, driving offences will earn drivers penalty points and face suspension of licences.
